question: On 15 October 2026, the European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) supported authorising Rasonque (daraxonrasib), a drug for adults with metastatic pancreatic cancer who have undergone systemic therapy at least once. The Agency added that it had forwarded its decision to the Commission, which will fast-track daraxonrasib’s authorisation procedure.

The WHO’s International Agency for Research on Cancer has estimated that more than 530 000 people were diagnosed with metastatic pancreatic cancer in 2024, and that this disease resulted in more than 490 000 deaths in that year alone. These figures highlight the severity of this disease and show just how urgent it is to open up more treatment options for patients.

The much-publicised case of the young Italian mother who was forced to look for alternatives highlights that time is very much a factor for patients living with metastatic pancreatic cancer. Daraxonrasib must be authorised as soon as possible, but without compromising the EU’s scientific and procedural safeguards. I therefore ask: 1.
In the light of the favourable opinion issued by the CHMP, is the Commission planning to authorise the placing of daraxonrasib on the EU market?
If this is indeed the case, what steps must be completed before such an authorisation can be issued, and how long does the Commission think that this process will take?
